summary: Air superiority and the intercept hour by hour, the frame every air order shares, what may fight what in the air, the shot of an air battle and where the loser goes.

addresses.name: AirMission_DayNightGate
addresses.signature: bool __cdecl AirMission_DayNightGate(CUnit* unit, int time, CMapProvince* province)
addresses.comment: **Whether an air mission may fly this hour.** IsNight for the province, the hour of the day and the month; with `time` 0 at night, or `time` 1 by day, the unit is stopped where it is at its base (CUnit::CancelMovement where it has a path) and otherwise its order is told to return to base, and the answer is no. Any other `time` flies day and night. So COrder +0x30 `time` is 0 day, 1 night, else both. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 1.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C, and the three pushes at 0x58A616..0x58A622 for the arguments.

addresses.name: CAirOrder::Start
addresses.comment: Slot 13 of an air order that has none of its own, and the first thing the others' do: a unit with a base that is not in its base's province is told to return to base. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 1.

addresses.name: CAirOrder::IsActive
addresses.comment: **Slot 14 of an air order, and the last thing the missions' own slot 14 asks.** No base: done. With `return_to_base` clear: the day and night gate; and, still clear and in no battle and no bombing, a unit whose range (definition +0x148) is under 1000 x CMap::DistanceBetweenProvinces(its base's province, the province it is in) is told to return **and the order is done**. With it set: in the base's province it is cleared and the order goes on while the tick is not past `death_date` (+0x2C); elsewhere, with no path and no battle, the return is ordered again. **So an order outlives its sorties, until its end date.** This is the clear at 0x58A6C4 that the naval write-up named. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 1.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C, and the listing 0x58A610..0x58A670 for the gate's arguments and the distance's.

addresses.name: CAirOrder::AddProvince
addresses.comment: Slot 36. Adds a province to the mission's list (+0x44) where slot 37 agrees and it is not there already. CSetOrderCommand::Execute calls it for each province of the command's `objectives` list. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 1.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C; the call through vftable[1] at slot 36 in CSetOrderCommand::Execute.

addresses.name: CAirOrder::IsProvinceInRange
addresses.comment: Slot 38, and slot 37 is a jump to it: COrder::IsTargetInRange for the order's unit and the province's id - within the unit's range of its base. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 1.

addresses.name: CAirOrder::FillArea
addresses.no_signature: thiscall with a pointer to the range and the province on the stack; its return was not read off the bytes.
addresses.comment: **Makes a mission's provinces out of a range.** From a province: mark it seen (CMapProvince +0x37C) and add it to the list where slot 38 agrees; then for each neighbour not seen, mark it, remember it on the list at +0x58, and where the unit's slot 35 (CanMoveTo) and the order's slot 38 agree and 1000 x the distance from the order's province to it is within the range, go on from it - for shape 3 only where an angle test passes (0x588E60, 0x589320, not read). The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 1.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C, and the listing 0x58954D..0x589563 for the distance's two provinces.

addresses.name: CAirOrder::SetAreaRange
addresses.comment: Stores the area's range (+0x74) and, for shape 2 or 3 (+0x6C), empties the mission's list and fills it again (CAirOrder::FillArea) from the order's province. The air window's `range_slider` calls it with the slider's value times the unit's range over 1000. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 1.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C; the table of three setters in CAirOrdersView slot 2 at 0x741DE0.

addresses.name: CAirOrder::SetAreaAngle
addresses.comment: Stores the area's angle (+0x70) and for shape 3 fills the mission's list again. The air window's `angle_slider`. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 1.

addresses.name: CAirOrder::SetAreaWidth
addresses.comment: Stores the area's width (+0x78) and for shape 3 fills the mission's list again. The air window's `width_slider`. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 1.

addresses.name: CAirPatrol::Start
addresses.comment: Slot 13 of air superiority: CAirOrder::Start's test, the mission's hour (CAirPatrol::UpdateMission), and a redraw of the mission map mode (0x12) where the unit is the player's. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 2.

addresses.name: CAirPatrol::IsActive
addresses.comment: Slot 14 of air superiority: no base, done; otherwise CAirPatrol::UpdateMission and then CAirOrder::IsActive. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 2.

addresses.name: CAirPatrol::UpdateMission
addresses.comment: **Air superiority's hour.** Nothing with `return_to_base` set, in a battle or with a path left; unfit (slot 25) or past its `death_date` it is told to return and the hour runs on; with no fuel received it is told to return and stops; the day and night gate. With no target, at its base and fit, it picks one (CAirPatrol::PickTarget); a target no longer in a province of the mission is dropped. With no destination and no target, or standing at its destination, the destination (+0x68, copied to +0xA8) becomes the province after it in the mission's list. In its target's own province it picks again and forgets its destination - or, past its date, returns. Otherwise it is given a way: to its destination with no target, **to the next province on its target's path** where the target is moving, else to the province the target is in. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C; the order is in EDI throughout.

addresses.name: CAirPatrol::PickTarget
addresses.comment: The enemy air unit air superiority goes for: over the mission's provinces the unit may stand in (slot 34) and its country knows at 2 or better (CMapProvince +0x370), every air unit of a country at war with it that has an order, scored by CAirPatrol::ScoreTarget; the highest above -10000, the first found among equals. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 2.

addresses.name: CAirPatrol::ScoreTarget
addresses.no_signature: The order, an out pointer and the candidate on the stack; the convention was not read off the bytes.
addresses.comment: -10,000,000 for a candidate with no order, at its own base (CUnit_IsAtOwnBase) or not an enemy where it is; and for one that enough are after already - the wings of every air unit at war with it whose order (slot 24 true) is an intercept or an air superiority with it for target, where that is above nothing and with the asking unit's own wings comes to more than 3. Otherwise the candidate's total strength (UnitSumStrength). The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 2.

addresses.name: ProvinceList_After
addresses.no_signature: The province arrives in EAX and the list in ESI.
addresses.comment: The province after a given one in a list, the first where none is given, the list is empty of it or it is the last: the given province in EAX, the list in ESI. Air superiority's round. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C, and the listing 0x59943F..0x599454 for the two registers.

addresses.name: CAirInterceptOrder::Start
addresses.comment: Slot 13 of the intercept: CAirOrder::Start's test, the watch set (CAirInterceptOrder::BuildWatchSet), CAirInterceptOrder::UpdateMission, and the redraw of the mission map mode. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 3.

addresses.name: CAirInterceptOrder::BuildWatchSet
addresses.comment: Fills the set at +0x80 with every province of the mission and, through AirIntercept_AddToWatchSet, every province within two steps of one. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 3.

addresses.name: AirIntercept_AddToWatchSet
addresses.signature: void __cdecl AirIntercept_AddToWatchSet(void* set, CMapProvince* province, int steps)
addresses.comment: Adds a province to the watch set and, while `steps` is above nothing, each neighbour not in it with one step less. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 3.

addresses.name: CAirInterceptOrder::PickTarget
addresses.comment: The enemy air unit the intercept goes for: over the watch set's provinces the unit may stand in and its country knows at 2 or better, every air unit of another country that is in a province of the mission - scored, and the best so far clears the meeting province (+0xC4) - or has one of the first three provinces of its path in the mission - scored, and the best so far sets the meeting province to it. Scored by CAirInterceptOrder::ScoreTarget. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 3.

addresses.name: CAirInterceptOrder::ScoreTarget
addresses.no_signature: The order, an out pointer and the candidate on the stack; the convention was not read off the bytes.
addresses.comment: CAirPatrol::ScoreTarget with one test more: a candidate with no wings is never picked. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 3.

addresses.name: CAirInterceptOrder::GoForTarget
addresses.comment: Gives the intercept its way: to the meeting province (+0xC4) where it has one and is not in it; otherwise, the target looked up by its id (+0xA0, +0xA4), to the next province on the target's path where the target is moving - nothing where that is the destination already - else to the province the target is in. The destination (+0x68) is set to where it goes. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 3.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C; the order is in EDI.

addresses.name: CAirCombatant::PickTarget
addresses.no_signature: The wing arrives in EAX, with the two combatants on the stack.
addresses.comment: **Which wing a wing fires at.** It keeps the target it remembers (CSubUnit +0xB8, +0xBC) while that object exists. Otherwise the other side's wings are collected (CAirCombatant::CollectTargets), its targeting skill is taken (CSubUnit::TargetingSkill), and `Random() % 100` is drawn: above a tenth of the skill a random one of the collected, `Random() % count`; else the best (CAirCombatant::BestTarget). None collected, or no best: no target, and the id is cleared. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 5.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C; the wing arrives in EAX.

addresses.name: CAirCombatant::BestTarget
addresses.no_signature: Two register arguments that are not used and two on the stack, answered as a pair in EDX:EAX.
addresses.comment: Over a combatant's collected targets, the highest of `priority x (250 + (max strength - strength) x 10 / 1000) x (1000 + targeting) / 1000`: the target's definition's priority (+0x194), and the firing wing's country's `bomber_targeting` (CTechnologyStatus +0xC8) where the target's definition has +0x37 set, its `fighter_targeting` (+0xCC) otherwise. The first among equals; one scoring nothing is never the best. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 5.

addresses.name: CAirCombatant::AddUnit
addresses.comment: Slot 12: CCombatant::AddUnit, and 1000 added for each wing of the unit to the count kept by unit type. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 5.

addresses.name: CAir::CanRetreatToProvince
addresses.comment: Slot 19 for an air unit: a province with no enemy air strength in it (EnemyAirStrengthIn under 1). CUnit::FindRetreatProvince asks it of a land neighbour - and then scores the neighbour nothing, so it decides nothing. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 6.

addresses.name: CUnit::GetAverageOrganisationShare
addresses.comment: Slot 26: the average over a unit's sub units of organisation x 1000 over the most each may have (CSubUnit::GetMaxOrganisation), in thousandths. CUnit::CheckOrderAndCombat sends an air unit away from its base home under a plain move where this is under the floor. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 6.

addresses.name: CUnit::GetTotalMaxStrength
addresses.comment: Slot 23: the sum of the sub units' definitions' `max_strength`. CAirOrder::IsFitToFly measures the unit's strength against it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 1.

addresses.name: CUnit::CanEngage
addresses.signature: char __stdcall CUnit::CanEngage(CUnit* this@EDI, CUnit* other@stack:4, bool bombing@stack:8, CMapProvince* province@stack:12) @AL
addresses.comment: **`this` is in EDI**, `ret 0xC`. The filter CCombatManager::StartCombat applies to each unit standing in the province before it will build a combat. After a war between the owners (or an undeclared one covering the province), different units and owners, neither retreating and - for a battle that is not a bombing - the same arm: **for two air units the orders count only at a base.** Where this unit is at its own base (CUnit_IsAtOwnBase) its order's slot 34 and slot 25 must both say yes; where the other is at its own base, **this** unit's order's slot 34 and the **other's** slot 25 must. Two units in the air may fight whatever their orders, which is how a bomber comes to be in an air combat; and a unit at its base that is unfit to fly cannot be fought. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 4.
addresses.revises: Said an air-to-air combat needs both orders to be air_intercept or air_superiority and both wings to pass IsFitToFly. The four calls are behind CUnit_IsAtOwnBase, and the second pair is this unit's slot 34 and the other's slot 25. The signature now places its stack arguments.

addresses.name: CAirCombatant::Attack
addresses.comment: **Slot 15 for an air fight.** After the leaders' hours and the practical's gain (AIR_DOCTRINE_INCREASE), for every wing of the side with an air attack (definition +0x140) and a target (CAirCombatant::PickTarget): n = air_attack x the wing's attack product (+0x50) / 1000; n / 1000 shots and one more where Random() % 100 is under the remainder's hundredths. Each shot, while the target's strength less its pending damage is not under nothing: a draw that is not used; missed where Random() % 100 is under CHANCE_TO_AVOID_HIT_AT_NO_DEF (99 at most); else organisation (Random() % AIR_COMBAT_ORG_DICE_SIZE + 1) x AIR_COMBAT_ORG_DAMAGE_MODIFIER and strength (Random() % AIR_COMBAT_STR_DICE_SIZE + 1), times AIR_COMBAT_CRITICAL_HIT_DAMAGE_MUL where Random() % 100 is under AIR_COMBAT_CRITICAL_HIT_DAMAGE_CHANCE, times AIR_COMBAT_STR_DAMAGE_MODIFIER; both times the two CAG modifiers where the target's definition is a carrier air group (+0x32); added to the target's pending organisation (+0xAC) and strength (+0xA8). **It never reads `air_defence`** or anything else of the target's. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 5.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C, the whole body.
addresses.revises: The comment only: it had the stats and defines read, and now has the loop, the draws in their order and the arithmetic.

addresses.name: CAirCombatant::CollectTargets
addresses.comment: Fills a combatant's `targets` (+0xB0, 1024 at most, the count at +0x10B0) with the other side's wings, in the order of its units and of each unit's wings: every wing whose strength less its pending damage - the pending strength over a hundred, as it will be settled - is not under nothing. `ret 4`, the other side in EAX. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 5.
addresses.revises: Was inferred, with the filter not stated.

addresses.name: CSubUnit::TargetingSkill
addresses.comment: Ten times the skill of the leader of the sub unit's unit, plus a technology figure of its owner: CTechnologyStatus +0x74 for a ship; for a wing `bomber_targeting` (+0xC8) and `fighter_targeting` (+0xCC) **added together**, whatever the wing or its target is. CSubUnit::PickTarget and CAirCombatant::PickTarget take a tenth of it as the chance in a hundred of the best target in place of a random one. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 5.
addresses.revises: The comment only: the wing's two figures are a sum, and the air caller is named.

addresses.name: CAirInterceptOrder::UpdateMission
addresses.comment: **The intercept's hour**, called from its slots 13 and 14. Nothing with a path left or in a battle; the day and night gate; nothing with `return_to_base` set. With fuel received, the tick not past `death_date` and fit to fly: at its meeting province (+0xC4) it picks again and goes; with no target it picks and goes only at its base; with a target outside the watch set it drops it and returns; with a target elsewhere than its own province it goes for it (CAirInterceptOrder::GoForTarget). **In every other case - no fuel, past its date, unfit, away from base with no target, or in its target's province - it is told to return to base.** See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 3.
addresses.revises: The comment only: the gates were listed and the mission's logic was not.

addresses.name: CAirCombat::Tick
addresses.comment: Slot 15 of the air combat and of the three bombings. A direct call to CCombat::Tick, and where that says the combat is over, the same; otherwise `duration (+0x20) >= 4` - **an air combat ends at its fourth hour unless the shared tick ends it sooner.** It makes no vftable call of its own; the combat modifiers are put on by CCombat::Tick through the combatants' slot 19, as for every arm. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 6.
addresses.evidence: reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airnaval.md, 'An air combat lasts four hours', which corrected this entry's claim in prose on 2026-10-04 without the entry following.
addresses.revises: Said it calls slots 15, 17 and 18 through the vftable and never the modifiers, so no air unit gets a modifier list. It calls CCombat::Tick, which applies them.

addresses.name: CUnit::FindRetreatProvince
addresses.comment:
**Where a unit falls back to**, or null when there is nowhere - which is what has CUnit::RetreatFromCombat remove it from the game instead.

Walks the provinces adjacent to the unit's own, over the path node's edge array (stride 0x14), and keeps the **best scoring** one. A candidate has to be passable and to pass the unit's virtual slot 13; its score is then built from *its* own neighbours:

- one under the unit owner's control, or passing the test at `0x0EFA00`, adds **1000**;
- one under nobody's enemy control adds **500** (g_RetreatNeutralNeighbourScore);
- **an enemy controlled neighbour halves the total** rather than adding to it.

The province is only taken if it scores above a floor, and the highest score wins. **Nothing qualifying means null**, and the unit is destroyed.

Rebels come first and separately: an owner tag of `REB` takes a path of its own which returns null outright unless `0x286C10` finds them somewhere with a flag at `+0x30`'s `+0x198` set.

**For an air unit** the neighbours are scored otherwise: a sea province 1000, and 2000 more for each land province beside it with a naval base that the unit may stand in; a land province nothing, which is never above the floor. And where no neighbour qualifies an air unit with a base goes to its base's province. So a beaten air unit beside the sea falls back out to sea. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 6.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C, 0x5C5F4F..0x5C63A7 and the last lines.
addresses.revises: The comment only: the air unit's arm is added.

struct_fields.name: area_seen
struct_fields.comment: The provinces CAirOrder::FillArea has marked seen (CMapProvince +0x37C), kept so that the marks can be cleared (0x589700) before the next fill. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 1.

struct_fields.name: area_shape
struct_fields.comment: The shape of the mission's area, one of the air window's four: 2 and 3 are filled by range, and 3 by angle and width as well. 0 and 1 were not read. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 1.

struct_fields.name: area_angle
struct_fields.comment: The air window's `angle_slider`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 1.

struct_fields.name: area_range
struct_fields.comment: The air window's `range_slider`, in the map's distance units: the slider's value times the unit's range over 1000. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 1.

struct_fields.name: area_width
struct_fields.comment: The air window's `width_slider`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 1.

struct_fields.name: no_battle_hours
struct_fields.comment: **The hours an air unit cannot be drawn into a battle.** CUnit::CheckOrderAndCombat writes 2 at its start where the unit is an air unit in a battle (0x5BA350) and takes one off at its end; CCombatManager::StartCombat and JoinCombatInProvince refuse a unit with it above nothing. So an air unit out of a battle has one hour in which it may move and cannot be fought. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 4.
struct_fields.evidence: The scan of 0x560000-0x5D2000 for dword writes at +0xA0, and the listing 0x5BA328..0x5BA356.

struct_fields.name: no_bombing_hours
struct_fields.comment: The twin of +0xA0 for a bombing: CUnit::CheckOrderAndCombat writes 2 where the unit is in one (+0x110, at 0x5BA335) and takes one off at its end. Its readers were not looked for; the name is by the likeness. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 4.
